```yaml
name: Cloud Dispatch Cleanup

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to clean up'
        required: true
        default: 'production'
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging
      dry_run:
        description: 'Dry run (no actual deletion)'
        required: false
        default: true
        type: boolean

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  cleanup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Authenticate with Cloud Provider
        uses: DataDog/dd-octo-sts-action@acaa02eee7e3bb0839e4272dacb37b8f3b58ba80
        with:
          domain: ${{ secrets.DD_DOMAIN }}
          audience: ${{ secrets.DD_AUDIENCE }}
          scope: ${{ secrets.DD_SCOPE }}
          policy: ${{ secrets.DD_POLICY }}

      - name: Run Cleanup Script
        env:
          CLOUD_TOKEN: ${{ steps.auth.outputs.token }}
          ENVIRONMENT: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          echo "Starting cleanup for environment: $ENVIRONMENT"
          echo "Dry run: $DRY_RUN"
          # Placeholder for actual cleanup logic
          # This would typically involve calling cloud provider APIs to remove stale assets
          # related to the Asset Manager regression fix
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Dry run mode: No assets were deleted."
          else
            echo "Executing cleanup..."
            # npm run cleanup:assets -- --env=$ENVIRONMENT
          fi
```
